Chemical Treatment: Triazole-based fungicides (e.g., Tebuconazole), Strobilurin fungicides (e.g., Azoxystrobin)
Immediate Action: Reduce canopy moisture and avoid overhead irrigation to prevent spore spreading.
Prevention: Planting resistant cultivars, Optimizing nitrogen fertilization to avoid lush, susceptible growth, Practicing effective crop rotation, Early field monitoring during high humidity periods

Symptoms: black powdery pustules on stems and leaves, ruptured epidermis
Organic Treatment: Crop rotation with non-host species, Removal and burning of infected crop residue, Use of resistant wheat varieties
Chemical Treatment: Triazole fungicides, Strobilurin fungicides, Propiconazole
Immediate Action: Apply systemic fungicides and minimize moisture in the field to slow spore germination.
Prevention: Planting resistant cultivars, Managing nitrogen application to prevent excessive canopy density, Strict sanitation of farm equipment, Monitoring weather patterns for high humidity and warm temperatures
